Article Title: Govt notifies Rs 3,030-crore scheme for three mega chemical parks
Article Text:
The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan) scheme, announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27, was cleared by the Cabinet chaired by PM Modi.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has formally notified the BHAVYA Rasayan scheme to establish three greenfield chemical parks across the country, paving the way for states to compete for projects aimed at boosting domestic chemical manufacturing, reducing import dependence and attracting investment.The Gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers operationalises the scheme approved by the Union Cabinet last month. With a total outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, the scheme will run from 2026-27 to 2030-31 and support the creation of shared industrial infrastructure for the chemical sector.Under the scheme, the Centre will provide up to Rs 1,000 crore for each chemical park, subject to the concerned state contributing at least Rs 500 crore. Any expenditure beyond this will have to be borne by the state government. Each park must have a minimum 8 sq km (2,000 acres) of contiguous, encumbrance-free land.The parks will be selected through a challenge-based competitive process, with proposals evaluated on predefined quantitative and qualitative parameters, including strategic relevance, financial viability, implementation plans and long-term sustainability.According to the notification, the parks will provide common facilities such as central effluent treatment plants, hazardous waste management systems, water supply, solvent recovery and distillation units, steam generation and distribution networks, interconnected pipelines, logistics infrastructure, laboratory testing centres and emergency response facilities, enabling industries to reduce costs and improve environmental compliance.The government said the scheme is aimed at strengthening the entire chemical value chain, enhancing domestic production capacity, improving cost competitiveness, promoting exports and import substitution, attracting domestic and foreign investment, and generating employment, while contributing to the goal of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Article Summary: The scheme will run from 2026-27 to 2030-31 and support the creation of shared industrial infrastructure for the chemical sector. Each park must have a minimum 8 sq km (2,000 acres) of contiguous, encumbrance-free land. The parks will be selected through a challenge-based competitive process.

Article Title: From New York to Delaware: US states to commemorate 'India Day' on August 15
Article Text:
US states proclaim August 15 as 'India Day' (representative image)

Delaware honours Indian-American community

New York, New Jersey also recognise August 15

How US communities celebrate India's Independence Day

India marks 80th Independence Day with focus on youth

Delaware has proclaimed August 15, 2026, as ‘India Day’, joining New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day and the contributions of the Indian-American community ahead of the country's 80th Independence Day.The proclamation was issued by Delaware Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community and its contributions to the state's social and economic life.The development was shared by the Consulate General of India in New York on August 13.According to the proclamation, Delaware is strengthened by the many cultures and traditions represented across its communities, including its Indian-American population.The proclamation said Delawareans of Indian heritage have enriched the state through their work, leadership and service, contributing to shared prosperity and creating opportunities for future generations.It also highlighted India's diversity of languages, traditions, faiths and customs, noting that generations of Indian Americans have carried these traditions forward while building communities in the US.The proclamation said India Day would provide an opportunity to honour India's independence, celebrate the heritage and achievements of Delaware's Indian-American community and recognise the enduring connections between Delaware and the people of India.Governor Meyer encouraged residents to participate in the observance and recognise the contributions of the state's Indian-American community.Delaware's proclamation follows similar declarations by New York and New Jersey, which recognised August 15, as India's Independence Day.New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill issued a proclamation recognising Indian Independence Day across the state. According to the Consulate General of India in New York, the proclamation highlighted the Indian-American community's contributions to New Jersey in areas including education, healthcare, research, technology, business, public service and community leadership.New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state.The Consulate said New York's proclamation recognised the Indian-American community's contribution to the state's cultural, economic and civic life, while also highlighting the enduring ties between India and the US.The Consulate thanked Hochul for the recognition, saying the proclamation celebrated India's journey of independence and the democratic values shared by the two countries.India's Independence Day is marked across the US each year through flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural programmes and community events.Indian diplomatic missions, including the Embassy of India in Washington and Indian consulates, hold special programmes on August 15. The Indian mission to the United Nations also participates in commemorative events.Indian-American communities across states organise cultural performances and public celebrations, with local political leaders often participating and highlighting the community's contributions to American society.Prominent landmarks have also joined the celebrations in previous years, including the Empire State Building in New York and the Space Needle in Seattle, which have been illuminated in the colours of the Indian tricolour for Independence Day events.The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.This year's celebrations will also focus on the commemoration of 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’, while placing particular emphasis on ‘Yuva Shakti’ or youth power.The celebrations are expected to combine the historical significance of India's freedom movement with recognition of the achievements and contributions of its younger generation.The growing number of US states formally recognising India's Independence Day also underlines the visibility of the Indian-American community and the broader social, economic and cultural ties between India and the United States.
Article Summary: Delaware joins New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day. Proclamation was issued by Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community. New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state. The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.

Article Title: Supreme Court pushes 19 states, union territories to notify cancer
Article Text:
Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting

NEW DELHI: With the National Cancer Registry Programme covering only a fraction of India’s population and rural cancer surveillance remaining particularly limited, the Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so, a move that could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.Such notification could help plug gaps in cancer surveillance by giving health authorities a more complete picture of the country’s cancer burden, including where cases are rising and which populations are most affected. The data could in turn help shape policies on prevention, early detection, treatment capacity and allocation of healthcare resources.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant passed the order on a plea filed by a retired AIIMS doctor after his lawyer Gaurav Bansal told the court that NCRP covers only 10% of population and rural coverage is less than 1%.The push assumes greater significance against the backdrop of the WHO’s latest Global Status Report on Cancer, which estimates that 92% of people globally will be affected by cancer either directly or through a close family member.The report also projects annual cancer cases to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050.The Supreme Court was informed that 17 of India’s 36 States and UTs have already notified cancer, following recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The remaining 19 have now been asked to consider similar action.Dr Pragya Shukla, Head of Clinical Oncology at Delhi State Cancer Institute, said standardised, disease-specific and timely data was essential to track India's changing cancer burden, identify regional and demographic trends, and assess the impact of prevention and treatment programmes. Such a system, she said, would complement existing cancer registries, help identify high-burden areas, improve planning for treatment infrastructure and medicines, and strengthen evidence-based cancer control. Govil added that reliable data would be critical for planning prevention, early detection and resource allocation.The Indian Cancer Society welcomed the intervention, saying national notification could help build a comprehensive cancer surveillance system. “The Supreme Court’s intervention is a significant development, and we welcome its direction to the remaining States and Union Territories to move towards cancer notification,” said Jyotsna Govil, Chairperson, Indian Cancer Society, Delhi. However, she stressed that notification alone would not suffice and called for a uniform national framework with common definitions, reporting standards and data protocols to ensure comparable and interoperable data across states.
Article Summary: Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so. The move could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.

Article Title: FSSAI puts influencers, celebrities on notice over food promotions
Article Text:
FSSAI warns influencers of legal action over unverified food claims

NEW DELHI: From "boosts immunity" to "rich in nutrients", food claims endorsed by celebrities and social media influencers are now under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) scanner. In a significant move aimed at curbing misleading promotions, the regulator has warned influencers and celebrities that endorsing unverified food claims could invite legal action, even as it cracked down on manufacturers selling unsafe food products.The advisory comes at a time when food brands are increasingly relying on digital creators and celebrities to market health drinks, protein supplements, snacks and packaged foods to millions of consumers online. FSSAI has asked influencers to verify that every claim made by a brand is truthful, scientifically substantiated and compliant with food safety regulations before lending their name or credibility.The regulator said endorsements are more than advertisements because consumers often trust the people promoting them. It cautioned influencers against amplifying claims such as "boosts immunity" or "rich in nutrients" unless they are backed by evidence and permitted under food laws.Misleading food advertisements and endorsements, it said, can attract action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.Alongside the advisory, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, sale and distribution of food products made by M/s Shree Shyam Foods, M/s Bharat Food Products and M/s KDP Food Industry after government laboratories found their ghee and mustard oil products unsafe for consumption.The regulator also penalised Dharwad Mishra Pedha and Food Processing Industry in Karnataka after its Motichoor laddoos were found to contain Tartrazine at 2,670.5 mg/kg, more than 26 times the permissible limit of 100 mg/kg. Shree Chemfood Pvt Ltd of Gujarat was similarly penalised after samples of iodised salt were found to be substandard and misbranded.FSSAI has also urged consumers to report misleading food advertisements and celebrity endorsements through its Food Safety Connect platform.
Article Summary: Food brands increasingly relying on digital creators and celebrities to market health drinks, protein supplements, snacks and packaged foods. FSSAI has asked influencers to verify that every claim made by a brand is truthful, scientifically substantiated and compliant with food safety regulations.

Article Title: Use medical tourists' money to treat poor Indians: Panel
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Revenue earned from foreign patients and affluent Indians should help fund treatment for poorer patients, a Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare has recommended, proposing that corporate hospitals adopt a cross-subsidisation model to make advanced healthcare more affordable.The panel said hospitals that benefit from government concessions such as subsidised land, tax incentives and 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) should earmark part of the revenue generated from medical tourism and high-paying patients to provide advanced tertiary care to economically weaker Indians.The recommendation is part of the committee's report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare, which noted that India's corporate hospital sector has recorded strong growth driven by high-value procedures, rising medical tourism and increasing revenue per occupied bed. While acknowledging India's emergence as a global healthcare destination, the panel said the benefits of this growth must also reach patients who cannot afford expensive treatment.Observing that private health insurance penetration in India remains low and out-of-pocket expenditure continues to push many families into financial distress, the committee said a structured cross-subsidy mechanism could improve access to life-saving tertiary care for poorer patients.It said hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections.The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY at standard package rates to ensure that beneficiaries have access to advanced treatment at leading private hospitals.To address the uneven distribution of healthcare infrastructure, the committee proposed linking government incentives, including subsidised land, tax benefits and FDI facilitation, to investment in tier-2, tier-3 and rural areas. It also recommended expanding public-private partnerships and extending financial and technology support to smaller hospitals in underserved regions.The recommendations form part of a broader roadmap to make healthcare more affordable. The committee has also proposed capping private hospital room rents in major metropolitan cities at the average tariff of nearby three-star hotels, standardising treatment package rates, improving price transparency and expanding government health spending to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure.
Article Summary: Hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections. The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY.

Article Title: NHAI tightens norms: Rs 10,000 fine if its ambulances fail to reach crash site in 10 minutes
Article Text:
There are around 3,000 ambulances and 1,000 patrol vehicles and cranes each covering nearly 50,000 km of highways under the NHAI

NEW DELHI: Ambulances deployed on NHs will face a Rs 10,000 penalty for failing to reach an incident site within 10 minutes, while a similar penalty will apply if they fail to take a victim to a hospital within the critical “golden hour”.National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) on Wednesday tightened the service-level agreements (SLAs) and key performance indicators (KPIs) for ambulances, cranes and patrolling vehicles deployed for incident management across the national highway network.There are around 3,000 ambulances and 1,000 patrol vehicles and cranes each covering nearly 50,000 km of highways under the NHAI.All these vehicles are equipped with GPS and dedicated mobile devices running the NHAI Care application, which relays crash-location information to response vehicles and records the action taken and other data during emergencies.Under the revised norms, a penalty of Rs 2,500 will be imposed if the NHAI Care app is unavailable in a vehicle for more than 1% of the time in a day. A similar penalty will apply if the vehicle’s GPS is not live.Govt has rolled out its helpline no 1033 across NH network to report any problem. In case of emergency, people get guided through this helpline number to book an ambulance. A dedicated 24X7 team issues tickets for ambulances, cranes and patrol vehicles for quick response.As per the new norm, if a vehicle delays in accepting a ticket within a minute, it will be liable to pay Rs 5,000 fine and rejecting to accept a ticket will cost Rs 10,000.It also specifies that every ambulance must do a 5 km dry run daily.Officials said the focus of the new norm is to ensure that these vehicles can swiftly come to anyone’s instance when required. NH stretches under NHAI accounted for 49,675 deaths in 2024, which was around one-fourth of all 1.77 road fatalities.Quick medical care can save 50% lives.
Article Summary: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) tightened the service-level agreements (SLAs) and key performance indicators (KPIs) for ambulances, cranes and patrolling vehicles deployed for incident management across the national highway network. There are around 3,000 ambulances and 1,000 patrol vehicles and cranes each covering nearly 50,000 km of highways under the NHAI.

Article Title: CPI data: Retail inflation moves up to 4.45% in July; stays above RBI's target for second month
Article Text:
Inflation remained higher in rural India at 4.84%, while urban areas registered a lower rate of 3.96%.

July 2026 CPI inflation: Retail inflation for the month of July edged up to 4.45%. The All India Consumer Price Index (CPI), with 2024 as the base year, recorded a provisional year-on-year inflation rate of 4.45% in July 2026 compared with July 2025. Inflation remained higher in rural India at 4.84%, while urban areas registered a lower rate of 3.96%.This is above RBI’s target of 4% but within the range of 2-6%. Inflation in June stood at 4.38%.Based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), provisional food inflation stood at 5.52% year-on-year in July 2026. Rural food inflation was estimated at 5.79%, whereas the corresponding rate for urban India was 5.05%.Housing inflation, measured on a year-on-year basis, was provisionally estimated at 2.22% in July 2026. Rural areas recorded housing inflation of 2.80%, while the urban housing inflation rate was lower at 2.01%.Earlier this month, the Reserve Bank of India had kept the policy rates unchanged while lowering the full year inflation forecast and raising its GDP growth projections.“The MPC noted that headline CPI inflation edged up above the target, as expected.The realised inflation for Q1, however, remained marginally lower than projections reflecting limited pass-through of cost pressures. The higher inflation is mostly on account of fuel and food with little signs of generalisation of price pressures so far. Core inflation excluding precious metals continues to be benign. As projected earlier, headline inflation is expected to rise further in the near term and peak in Q3:2026-27, primarily due to food and fuel, before moderating thereafter,” RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said in his policy statement.“Going forward, El Niño’s impact on temporal and spatial rainfall distribution continues to remain a major risk, although proactive supply management and adequate stock of foodgrains should provide comfort. Global oil prices have remained highly volatile with sharp two-way movements triggered by geopolitical developments, blurring the near-term outlook. Although generalised inflation pressures continue to remain modest so far, the risks of second-round impact of higher food, fuel and other input prices translating to broad-based inflation persist,” he said.“After considering all factors, CPI inflation for 2026-27 is projected to be 5.0 per cent with Q2 at 4.7 per cent; Q3 at 5.9 per cent; and Q4 at 5.5 per cent. Inflation for Q1:2027-28 is projected at 5.3 per cent with risks being evenly balanced. Core inflation is projected at 4.3 per cent for 2026-27. Core inflation excluding precious metals is projected to be lower, though it is likely to align with core inflation from Q4,” he added.
Article Summary: The All India Consumer Price Index (CPI), with 2024 as the base year, recorded a provisional year-on-year inflation rate of 4.45% in July 2026. Inflation remained higher in rural India at 4.84%, while urban areas registered a lower rate of 3.96%. This is above RBI’s target of 4% but within the range of 2-6%.

NEW DELHI: CPM MP John Brittas has moved a privilege motion against BJP MP Sushmita Dev, alleging that she addressed him as “lungiwala” during proceedings in Rajya Sabha Monday. Dev denied that she had cast aspersions on attire of any state.Brittas raised the issue in the House Wednesday after listed papers were laid on the table at the start of the day. Article Title: ‘Charges proved’: Lok Sabha panel for action against Justice Yashwant Varma
Article Text:
The report by the committee headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar was tabled in Lok Sabha Wednesday

Also read:

Judge's testimony evasive, misleading: Parl panel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Speaker appointed inquiry committee in its report has recommended further action while indicting Justice Yashwant Varma for recovery of wads of 500-rupee notes at his official residence in Delhi in March last year, its unexplained disappearance and an evasive judge failing to explain "presence, source or ownership" of the huge money.The report by the committee headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar, which was tabled in LS Wednesday, recommended "such further action as may be considered in accordance with law" against Justice Varma, who withdrew from inquiry proceedings after failing to come up with convincing replies to questions put to him and, in what was seen as a move to pre-empt his removal by Parliament, resigned as Allahabad High Court judge.What shape the "action" recommended by the committee might take is not clear but sources did not rule out the possibility of Parliament initiating removal proceedings against Justice Varma despite his resignation. A CBI inquiry was also being discussed as a possible course of action.The committee said Justice Varma's explanation for the pile of cash "remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against evidence of independent official witnesses and corroborative material" and returned a finding that all three charges against the judge stood proved.Justice Yashwant Varma's reply to Delhi HC Chief Justice on March 22, 2025 - a week after the fire incident that led to discovery of huge cash at his official residence - and his subsequent stand "did not exhibit the candour, transparency and institutional responsibility expected in the circumstances", the Lok Sabha Speaker appointed inquiry committee said in its 121-page, 299-paragraph report.On the judge's testimony, the committee said, "It was evasive because it did not engage with the central circumstance of substantial currency notes seen by independent officials inside the storeroom. It was incomplete because it did not disclose the factual steps allegedly taken by him, the details of inquiries made, the answers received from staff or household members, or any action taken to preserve the site.. . It was misleading in effect because the earliest broad denial gave way to successive alternative hypotheses, none of which was substantiated when opportunity to lead defence evidence was available." On Justice Varma's decision to withdraw from inquiry proceedings and resign from judgeship, the committee said the judge withdrew at a stage when he was required to substantiate with evidence his theories relating to foul play, planting of money and possible role of staff. "He did not lead evidence to substantiate them," it said. The committee recorded the shifting shape of the defence put forth by Justice Varma. "The defence moved from denial of presence to absence of seizure and verification, to possible fake currency notes, to possible removal by first responders, and to suspicions regarding staff. Each of these hypotheses required some factual foundation if it was to displace the evidence of independent official witnesses and the corroborative electronic material," it said.By alleging that the first responders had removed the burnt currency notes, the judge admitted these were at the storeroom inside his residential premises, the committee said, referring his writ petition in SC in which he had indirectly admitted to presence of cash at his residential premises."No satisfactory explanation has been furnished as to how currency notes seen by several official witnesses disappeared or became unavailable. These facts establish failure to preserve...material evidence," it said."What stands established is that substantial unexplained currency notes were found within the official premises occupied by the judge..."it said.The report may come up for discussion in Parliament's next session, and a further course of action against Varma will then be decided.
Article Summary: The Lok Sabha Speaker appointed inquiry committee in its report has recommended further action while indicting Justice Yashwant Varma. The committee said Justice Varma's explanation for the pile of cash "remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against evidence of independent official witnesses and corroborative material"

Article Title: How difficult is it to become a doctor or an engineer in India?
Article Text:

What government told in Parliament

Level of competition

For a very long time, anyone considered particularly good at studies in India was almost automatically tipped to become a doctor or an engineer.made a joke of that national fixation years ago, showing a world in which parents and professors seemed convinced they knew what success ought to look like.Alternative streams of education have slowly gained popularity since then. The race to become a doctor or engineer, however, has hardly become easier. As the pool of aspirants expands beyond the metros, competition for a coveted seat has only become harder. Many tuition centres, almost like factories, in Kota and other places train students rigorously to pass these coveted exams.The May 3 NEET-UG examination was cancelled after the paper-leak controversy and nearly 20 lakh candidates returned for a re-examination on June 21. The anger travelled from coaching rooms to Ja nta r Mantar and towards Parliament, propelled by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party. Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister on July 25. The CBI chargesheet has since named 13 accused, including three subject experts associated with NTA, while CJP has demanded that the testing agency itself be replaced. Similar protests over exam leaks have now erupted in Jharkhand.The anger that erupted at Jantar Mantar after the leak is merely a reflection of the deeper anxiety over competition for quality jobs and the yearning for a stronger CV, which for many begins with studying at a hallowed institution. How difficult, then, is it to get into a top-tier engineering or medical college in India?Engineering here means the route to the country's most sought-after public engineering institutions, particularly the IITs and NITs, not every engineering college.The pathways are slightly different. JEE Main is the direct gateway to the 31 NITs participating in JoSAA 2026, while it also acts as the screening stage for candidates hoping to reach the IITs through JEE Advanced.NTA recorded 15,38,468 unique candidates appearing for JEE Main 2026. Of the 1,87,389 who registered for JEE Advanced, 1,79,694 appeared in both papers and 56,880 qualified. The JoSAA 2026 matrix provides 18,826 IIT seats.Put another way, the original Main candidate pool is roughly 82 times the number of IIT seats. Even after reaching JEE Advanced, there were 9.5 test-takers and almost exactly three qualifiers for every IIT place.Not every JEE Main candidate is a serious IIT contender, so the 82-to-one comparison is largely academic. It is a measure of the scale of the field, not an individual's admission probability. Seats are allocated across categories and other reservation rules. But in both IITs and NITs, the fight is not only for a seat, but also for a preferred stream and college.Interest in admission wanes considerably as one goes down the value chain. That distinction becomes clearer when one looks at the rest of India's engineering system. The latest Rajya Sabha disclosure by the ministry states that BTech/BE enrolment in AICTE-approved institutions rose to 13.56 lakh in 2025-26. Yet adding up the state-wise vacancies in the same annexure produces 2,52,914 empty seats. In the same year, 67 AICTE-approved engineering and technology institutions applied for closure or were listed as closed. So India does not lack engineering seats. What it lacks are the seats students value most in IITs, top NITs and other highly sought-after institutions.The engineering race does not necessarily end with a BTech for all. For those aiming for an MTech from an IIT, NIT or another premier institution, GATE becomes another competitive gate.The numbers are substantial. In GATE 2026, 2,11,020 candidates appeared for the Computer Science and Information Technology paper, while 95,752 appeared for Electronics and Communication, 76,385 for Civil Engineering and 69,242 for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.Those figures cannot simply be converted into applicants-per-MTech-seat ratios. Candidates can sit more than one GATE paper. For NITs, the pool is still broader. CCMT 2026 accepts valid GATE scores from 2024, 2025 and 2026. So candidates for these seats can effectively be competing with more than one year's GATE cohort. However, suffice to say, the odds are tough for aspirants.Medical education runs on the same preference for high-value seats. For the valid June 21 NEET re-examination, 22,79,743 candidates were registered, 19,99,895 appeared and 11,21,185 qualified. The cancellation itself affected the denominator, with 2,79,848 registered candidates not sitting the re-test.Against this pool, the NMC's July matrix lists 1,36,939 MBBS seats for 2026-27, excluding Institutes of National Importance such as AIIMS. The NEET test-taker pool is about 14.6 times the listed MBBS capacity, while the number of qualified candidates is about 8.2 times the capacity. These are broad national comparisons, not individual admission odds, since seats are divided across quotas, categories and state eligibility rules. But the headline number conceals another hierarchy.Of those 1,36,939 NMC-listed seats, 63,296 are in government colleges and 73,643 are private. Private colleges account for about 54% of the listed capacity. If we compare the NEET re-test pool only with NMC-listed government seats, the candidate pool is roughly 31.6 times the available government capacity.Government seats are prized because of substantially greater affordability, the reputation of established institutions and, in many large public hospitals, the prospect of extensive clinical exposure. This year's expansion makes that distinction sharper. NMC approved 9,911 additional MBBS seats for 2026-27. Of these, 7,800 are private and only 2,111 government.Nearly four out of every five newly approved seats were added on the private side. So medicine and engineering are more alike than they look. In both, the real contest is increasingly over which seat, in which institution, and at what cost. There is, however, an important difference between the engineering and medical journeys.An engineer can enter another fierce competition through GATE for MTech, but postgraduate study remains an optional route for most. For doctors who want to specialise, postgraduate training is much closer to another necessary career gate.The latest completed NEET-PG examination makes the scale clear. More than 2.42 lakh candidates appeared for NEET-PG 2025, according to the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences. NEET-PG 2026 is yet to be held and is scheduled for August 30.And the postgraduate pool is much smaller than the undergraduate universe. The Centre said in July that India had 86,360 postgraduate medical seats in 2025-26. Earlier this year, it said 8,967 additional PG seats, including those in AIIMS and other Institutes of National Importance, had been approved for 2025-26. For some who pursue super-specialisation, there may still be another competitive gate beyond that.Governments have tried to accommodate more students in quality institutions. Seven IITs have been established since 2014, while approved expansion at five newer IITs is intended to create capacity for another 6,500 students. In medicine, 157 government medical colleges have been approved under one central scheme, with 137 already functional. Separate government programmes have also expanded undergraduate and postgraduate capacity.But adding seats does not automatically solve the problem. The latest figures placed before Parliament show 15.35 lakh registered allopathic doctors and 7.52 lakh AYUSH practitioners and, assuming 80% availability in both groups, a government-estimated combined practitioner-population ratio of 1:778. Yet the existence of incentives for hard-to-serve areas underlines another problem. Doctors and specialists are not distributed evenly. So hierarchy exists beyond educational institutions too, which makes the work of policymakers even harder in a large country like India.In the US, 54,699 people applied to MD-granting medical schools in 2025 and 23,440 matriculated, but candidates generally apply after or during undergraduate study and typically take the MCAT. In England, medicine remains one of the most competitive university routes, with a sizeable socioeconomic gap in acceptance rates.France pushes much of the filter inside university, with two in five students entering its PASS or L.AS health routes in 2022 reaching medicine or another major health discipline within two years. China's Gaokao had 1.29 crore registrations in 2026, but admissions are distributed across provinces, universities and programmes rather than through a single NEET-style medicine pool. Russia uses another lever altogether, with targeted state-funded medical training linked to future employment and workforce.Every country has tried different approaches based on the reality of the land. Whether a test like NEET is the best way forward is still being intensely debated. However, for policymakers, the only feasible solution seems to be building more institutions of comparable quality, ones students believe can offer strong education, credible employment prospects and a better quality of life. Simply multiplying seats is unlikely to be enough if aspirants continue to see only a small proportion of them as worth fighting for.
Article Summary: The race to become a doctor or engineer has hardly become easier. As the pool of aspirants expands beyond the metros, competition for a coveted seat has only become harder. Many tuition centres, almost like factories, in Kota and other places train students rigorously to pass coveted exams.

Article Title: After 26 yrs & SC order, Shaurya Chakra awardee’s widow gets rightful pension
Article Text:
These are not matters where the family or the widow should be expected to go to the court to obtain relief, Supreme Court said

NEW DELHI: Official apathy sometimes doesn’t spare even the families of those who lay down their lives for the country. A case in point is the decades-long struggle of the widow of ‘Shaurya Chakra’ awardee Mohan Singh, who had to wait for 26 years to get her rightful Special Family Pension — that too only after the Supreme Court’s intervention.Singh, an overseer with General Reserves Engineering Force, was in charge of construction of a key border road. On July 10, 2000, when a boulder from a hilltop rolled down with debris, he helped move workers from the site but could not get out of its way himself and was killed. The Centre posthumously conferred on him in 2001 the ‘Shaurya Chakra’ — the third-highest peacetime gallantry award.However, his widow received relief under Workmen’s Compensation Act and not the Special Family Pension under the CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, to which she was entitled. It was rejected on the ground that since payment under Workmen’s Compensation Act had been made, no liberalised pensionary award was due to the deceased’s kin, as per CCS (Pension) rules.She moved Punjab and Haryana HC, which held she was entitled to extraordinary pension but restricted payment of arrears from date of the filing of petition, denying relief from the date of death of her husband. When the matter reached the SC, a bench of Justices K V Viswanathan and Arun Palli said the Centre had erred and should have categorised her case under the correct category ‘C’ of CCS Pension Rules and extended the benefit soon after Singh’s demise.“These are not matters where the family or the widow should be expected to go to the court to obtain relief,” SC said.AG R Venkataramani said Rs 14.28 lakh had been paid to the widow and pension will be processed as per HC order. Arrears, calculated at Rs 4.12 lakh, had also been released. SC said a consolidated amount of Rs 10 lakh be paid to her for the period between Singh’s death and HC order.
Article Summary: Mohan Singh, an overseer with General Reserves Engineering Force, was in charge of construction of a key border road. On July 10, 2000, when a boulder from a hilltop rolled down with debris, he helped move workers from the site but could not get out of its way himself. NEW DELHI: A week after criticising long delay in trial of a Popular Front of India (PFI) activist facing UAPA charges by asserting that “lifespan of a criminal trial cannot be that of a turtle”, Supreme Court on Wednesday again slammed the Karnataka govt for submitting a prosecution plan “as absurd as a fairytale”.Mindful of the trend of UAPA trials lingering indefinitely, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said no special court, set up to conduct trial of UAPA cases, should be saddled with more than 12-15 cases. The directive came as the bench found that the prosecution was yet to start producing its witnesses despite having cited 700 of them. The accused, a functionary of the outlawed hardline Islamist group PFI, has been in jail for four years. The SC on Aug 5 asked the state govt to submit a prosecution plan specifying how many protected witnesses were to be examined and within what timeframe.Karnataka’s counsel Rooh-e-Hina Dua said the state intended to examine three protected witnesses and 50 other witnesses against the petitioner Shahid Khan and said it could take a year for the prosecution to complete its evidence and examination of witnesses.The bench said, “It shows the lackadaisical approach of the state.The prosecution does not give a clear picture of the trial process when the accused is languishing in jail for nearly four years without a trial.”For the petitioner, who was arrested on Sept 22, 2022, for allegedly radicalising youth and being involved in violent activities, senior advocate Aditya Sondhi said the HC rejected his bail plea without considering the right to liberty and right to expeditious trial.The bench said the charges against the petitioner were serious and directed the prosecution to complete examination of the three protected witnesses in three months. It asked the prosecution, the petitioner and the co-accused, who are on bail, not to repeatedly file applications.The petitioner is accused of helping raise funds for PFI between 2011 and 2019 and helping teams of the banned outfit which had planned attacks in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala against CAA and NRC, and judgement relating to hijab and Babri demolition.
Article Summary: Supreme Court criticises long delay in trial of a Popular Front of India (PFI) activist facing UAPA charges. The accused, a functionary of the outlawed hardline Islamist group PFI, has been in jail for four years.

Article Title: Phuket-Delhi Air India pilot fails 2nd dope test, was high on marijuana
Article Text:
Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances.

Airbus A320 had momentarily gone into ‘negative G’ situation

What happened on board

What govt is doing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What it means for AI

NEW DELHI: Trouble mounted for the pilot-in-command (PIC) of last Tuesday’s badly rattled Phuket-Delhi Air India flight after it emerged that he had failed the confirmatory dope test and was found to have consumed marijuana. Besides, the cabin crew of the flight, AI 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high” PIC’s onboard behaviour.The pilot also faces criminal action beyond DGCA rules — which require such a pilot to be sent for de-addiction and allow him to resume flying after being certified drug-free.The young co-pilot had to single-handedly steady the aircraft and then land it safely at the destination.An alarmed civil aviation ministry summoned AI’s outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson to express concern about this incident and find out how the airline was dealing with the issue and review its plan to come out of its prolonged period of operational turbulence.The incident that has raised questions over the robustness of the Indian system has also pushed DGCA to explore ways to make dope test rules more stringent after the incident that left 20 passengers and four cabin crew members injured.“Certain records, statements, medical information and other material collected during the investigation are protected and confidential in accordance with the applicable investigation framework….AAIB (Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau) requests all concerned to respect the investigation process and refrain from drawing conclusions… AAIB will conduct a thorough investigation covering all material facts and relevant evidence and will issue its preliminary findings,” the aviation ministry said in a statement while responding to queries on the confirmatory test.Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances. “He was often sitting on the floor of the flight deck and tried to smoke out. Cabin crew had to help him back to his seat. He was not in full control of himself. He was unable to walk properly after exiting the aircraft,” said a person in the know. AI did not comment on the cabin crew’s alleged complaints.The probe will determine whether the aircraft had a sudden loss of altitude due to a series of multiple and rare technical snags, which have been reported by the co-pilot in his report, or it was caused by actions of the PIC.When the aircraft experienced loss of altitude, the PIC is learnt to have been standing and leaning behind the co-pilot’s seat. The Airbus A320 had momentarily gone into a “negative G” situation when the PIC and things in the cockpit floated up and those who were not wearing seat belts got injured in the passenger cabin.Also read: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government The cabin crew have given a report to AI. The co-pilot may have informed the airline’s ground control about the pilot’s behaviour due to which the unusual step of subjecting the cockpit crew to a drug test — instead of just breath analyser tests — was taken.“AAIB is engaged in systematic collection, preservation and examination of all relevant technical, operational, medical and human-factor evidence,” the govt said.While DGCA is reviewing its rule titled “procedure for examination of aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances”, India’s senior-most pilots sought a differentiation between a pilot testing positive after having a medication for sleeping or anxiety and those who are found to have consumed “true” psychoactive substances.Airlines have a list of medicines that need to be avoided some hours before flight as they can cause drowsiness.Massive financial losses apart, the airline’s operations and training are again under a cloud, just when it was trying to regain public faith following the Ahmedabad crash in June 2025.While Tatas and partner Singapore Airlines have pumped in thousands of crores and there have been significant cosmetic improvements, it is still looking for leadership and professional management that can usher in the culture required to fly it out of turbulence.
Article Summary: Trouble mounted for the pilot-in-command (PIC) of last Tuesday’s badly rattled Phuket-Delhi Air India flight. It emerged that he had failed the confirmatory dope test and was found to have consumed marijuana. The cabin crew of the flight, AI 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high’ PIC's onboard behaviour.

NEW DELHI: A national-level sportswoman, employed as a safaiwala (group D employee) in railways since 2003, has been awaiting promotion to group C level for last two decades despite the railway ministry’s policy to grant out-of-turn first promotion to medal-winning employees, a criterion she had fulfilled by winning two medals in national events.A decade after winning medals but not getting promotion as per the policy, Rajni Rani moved Punjab and Haryana HC in 2016 with a writ petition, which got dismissed on technical grounds. Her appeal against the HC order has been pending in SC since Nov 2016.It was last heard on Jan 9, 2017, when a bench of Justices J Chelameswar and A M Sapre admitted her petition and asked the Union govt to file a response in eight weeks. On May 15, 2018, registrar Kapil Mehta had recorded that statement of case had not been filed by any of the parties despite expiry of the time granted. He had asked for the case to be listed before the court as per rules. However, her petition continued to gather dust till her counsel Wednesday requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant for an early hearing. A visibly unhappy CJI directed the registry to list the petition for hearing on Aug 21.Rajni said she was due for promotion in 2005 after winning medals but was denied the benefit of first promotion on the ground that one of the four events she had participated in did not qualify as a national event. She said the rules prescribed participation in only two events. Rajni said she had won a bronze medal at 52nd Northern Railway Athletic Meet in Feb 2005, gold medal at 44th Senior National Inter-State competition in July 2004 and represented railways in open National in Mumbai in Sept 2004, securing fourth position.Rajni was denied a promotion in 2013 despite a directive by Central Administrative Tribunal to railways in Sept 2012 to consider her case. When she challenged the decision, both CAT and HC dismissed her petitions.
Article Summary: Rajni Rani is a national-level sportswoman, employed as a safaiwala (group D employee) in railways since 2003. She has been awaiting promotion to group C level for last two decades despite the railway ministry’s policy to grant out- of-turn first promotion to medal-winning employees.

Article Title: 5 indigenous small modular reactors targeted by 2033, Jitendra Singh tells LS
Article Text:
Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A key objective of the govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033, minister for department of atomic energy Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a high temperature gas cooled reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MW capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.Singh said India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, SMRs, domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the country’s abundant thorium resources. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of SMRs at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.The minister also highlighted continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for sodium cooled fast breeder reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of India’s long-term nuclear strategy.On thorium, Singh said India is pursuing its three-stage nuclear power programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam. Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.
Article Summary: The govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition.

Article Title: IN-SPACe approved country’s first fully commercial earth observation sat constellation: Jitendra Singh
Article Text:
The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India and includes Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India

NEW DELHI: Space regulator IN-SPACe has approved and signed under the PPP model an agreement with a private consortium for the country’s first indigenous, fully commercial earth observation constellation, with a view to enhancing the country’s space-based observation capabilities and building a self-reliant earth observation (EO) ecosystem in the country, minister for department of space Jitendra Singh informed Lok Sabha on Wednesday in response to a Parliament question.The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India and includes Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India. It will invest more than Rs 1,200 crore for setting up the constellation, which is to be developed and operationalised by 2029.The consortium will design, build, own and operate the 12-satellite constellation, which will have panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities, supported by indigenous ground infrastructure. All satellites are to be manufactured domestically and launched on Indian launch vehicles, with mission control based in the country.The programme includes designing, fabrication, integration and the testing of EO satellites, including five ultra-high resolution optical satellites with 4 bands, 3 multispectral satellites with 8 bands, 2 hyperspectral optical satellites with 250 bands and 2 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites in X-band, by the Indian industry. The EO programme will use Indian launch vehicles (either private or Isro facilities) for placing the satellites into orbit. The programme also allows collaboration with academic and research institutions for capacity building and application development, the minister said.
Article Summary: The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India. It will invest more than Rs 1,200 crore for setting up the constellation, which is to be developed and operationalised by 2029. All satellites are to be manufactured domestically and launched on Indian launch vehicles, with mission control based in the country.

NEW DELHI: The Joint Action Forum on Minorities that had led a delegation of representatives of Churches to meet Home Minister Amit Shah last week described the decision of the govt to refer the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 to a Joint Parliamentary Committee as a “positive step” that presents an “important opportunity for a comprehensive, clause-by-clause review of its provisions and their implications”.A host of Church bodies last week met and urged home minister Amit Shah to either withdraw the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill or send it to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.In their representation to HM, the delegation representing Catholic, Protestant and Orthodox Churches from across India organised under Joint Action Forum on Minorities with DMK MP P Wilson as its chairperson, had sought that the Bill is withdrawn in entirety or in alternate be referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee together with a review of the working of the Principal FCRA Act 2010 itself".On Wednesday, Wilson in a statement on X thanked DMK President MK Stalin and all opposition parties in the Lok Sabha for their unified demand to withdraw the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, even though it was decided by a majority voice vote to refer it to the Joint Parliamentary Committee.“Although the govt has not agreed to withdraw the FCRA Bill 2026 entirely, the Union Government's decision to refer the Bill to the Joint Parliamentary Committee is a positive step,” he added.“This is a sensitive issue where a balance must be struck between the govt’s authority over financial control and the rights of minority institutions to receive charitable contributions. This funding supports schools, colleges, hospitals, and other public service institutions. The government will be unable to fund these activities if contributions cease,” he added.Wilson said that the referral of the Bill to the JPC presents an important opportunity for a comprehensive, clause-by-clause review of its provisions and their implications. “We hope and expect that the Committee will listen to all stakeholders and carefully consider the constitutional, legal, and practical concerns raised by religious, educational, healthcare, charitable, and civil society institutions,” he said.The National Council of Churches in India, General Secretary, Asir Ebenezer welcomed the Bill and said that they look forward to engaging with “the JPC as they prepare the report for the Winter session”. NCCI was part of the delegation that met the HM as part of the Joint Action Forum on Minorities.“On behalf of the historic and nationally networked Protestant and Orthodox Churches in India representing the religious and mission aspirations of 19 million Christians we thank the Home Minister and the govt for heeding to the request of the Christian community,” he added.
Article Summary: A host of Church bodies last week met and urged home minister Amit Shah to either withdraw the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill or send it to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny. The decision to refer the bill to JPC was made by a voice vote.

NEW DELHI: If citizens have a fundamental right to assemble and protest peacefully, should it interfere with fundamental rights of those who are not part of the protest to commute safely to their offices or go about their daily lives?This conflict of fundamental rights of protesters and other citizens was highlighted by advocate V Elanchezian, who appeared for PIL petitioner Aalok Mohan, and requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant to direct govt to frame a model national framework for providing facilities and guidelines for regulating protests so that they don't interfere with the rights of others.Citing population growth and urbanisation, the petitioner said, "Despite these developments, there exists no comprehensive national framework prescribing minimum planning standards for infrastructure relating to peaceful public assemblies. Consequently, public authorities across the country adopt differing administrative practices, often leading to avoidable conflict between the constitutional rights of demonstrators and those of commuters, patients, school children, emergency services and the public. ""The issue is not whether citizens have the right to assemble peacefully, for that right is protected by the Constitution. The issue is whether constitutional governance now requires govt to examine and formulate a comprehensive national policy providing minimum standards for planning and developing civic infrastructure that facilitates peaceful public assemblies while ensuring harmonious protection of all Fundamental Rights," the petition said.The bench said it would consider the issue flagged by the petitioner along with other pending petitions seeking identification of proper protest sites with basic amenities, including water, washroom, food and medical assistance, so as not to inconvenience or impede daily commuters from reaching their workplaces or destinations on time.
Article Summary: SC to consider identifying protest sites that won’t affect daily commute of people. Petitioner V El Sanchezian, who appeared for PIL petitioner Aalok Mohan, requested a bench to direct govt to frame a model national framework for providing facilities and guidelines for regulating protests.

Article Title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann meets Governor; seeks 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on "humanitarian grounds"
Article Text:
Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann meets Governor; seeks 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on "humanitarian grounds"

Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday met with the Governor to recommend a 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on humanitarian grounds, citing the deteriorating health of the prisoner's mother.Jagtar Singh Hawara is currently serving a life sentence for his involvement in the 1995 assassination of the then Punjab chief minister Beant Singh.Speaking to the media after the meeting, the chief minister stated that the recommendation was made to allow Hawara to meet his mother, who has not seen him in over three decades."A recommendation was made recently regarding the matter of granting parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara so that, on humanitarian grounds, he could be given parole as his mother's health is not well. His mother has a desire to meet him after 31 years," CM Mann said.The chief minister explained that since the case is being heard in the Union Territory, the Governor's role is pivotal in forwarding the request to the Central Government."I met the Governor today because as the case is being heard in the UT, the Governor will have an important role and the matter will be sent to the Centre. The final decision rests with the Centre, but we have requested a 10-day parole," he added.Addressing potential concerns regarding security and public order, CM Mann informed that he has provided a formal assurance to the administration."In this regard, we have assured the Governor that we will not allow the atmosphere to be spoiled in any way and the situation will remain under control," the CM asserted.According to the chief minister, the Governor has responded positively to the request and promised to expedite the administrative formalities."The Governor has assured that he will speak with the Home Secretary of the Government of India today itself to complete the formalities, and Hawara will receive relief soon. The Punjab government will send whatever necessary documents are required from their side," Mann stated.Earlier on August 9, CM Mann wrote to Governor Gulab Chand Kataria regarding the same."It has been brought to my notice that Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara's mother is not in good health due to age-related health problems. Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara has also filed CRWP No. 3868/2026 in the Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chandigarh, seeking direction to release him on parole. The Hon'ble Court has also directed to consider his parole application. Therefore, on the basis of human compassion, I would like to request you to grant 10-day parole as soon as possible," the letter read.
Article Summary: Jagtar Singh Hawara is currently serving a life sentence for his involvement in the 1995 assassination of the then Punjab chief minister Beant Singh. Punjab CM Bhagwant Singh Mann met with the Governor to recommend a 10-day parole for Hawara on humanitarian grounds.

Article Title: Assam floods: Toll rises to 103; 87,000 remain affected in four districts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The flood situation in Assam showed signs of improvement on Wednesday, with the number of people affected falling to around 87,000 across four districts. However, the death toll from this year's floods rose to 103 after two more people died in the past 24 hours.The latest figures from the Assam State Disaster Management Authority showed that one person drowned in Sivasagar and another in Karbi Anglong.Around 86,800 people are still affected by the floods in Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Sivasagar. Golaghat remains the worst-hit district, with more than 42,000 people affected. Nagaon has around 20,000 affected residents, while Sivasagar has about 15,000.The situation has nevertheless improved compared with Tuesday, when nearly 1.13 lakh people were affected across the four districts.Authorities are continuing relief operations in the affected areas. A total of 79 relief camps and distribution centres are currently operating across five districts, providing assistance to 13,011 people.Over the past 24 hours, relief agencies distributed nearly 96.55 quintals of rice, 18.26 quintals of dal, 5.41 quintals of salt and more than 204 litres of mustard oil among flood-affected families.Despite the improvement, the floods continue to damage homes, farmland and infrastructure.According to ASDMA, 433 villages remain underwater, while more than 10,884 hectares of crop land have been damaged across the state.Floodwaters have also damaged embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure in several districts.The Dhansiri River at Numaligarh continues to flow above the danger mark, adding to concerns in the affected areas.The floods have also affected livestock. More than 32,900 domestic animals and poultry have been impacted across Assam.While the overall number of people affected has declined, the rising death toll and continuing damage to villages, farmland and infrastructure show that the flood crisis is far from over.
Article Summary: Around 86,800 people are still affected by the floods in Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Sivasagar. The death toll from this year's floods rose to 103 after two more people died in the past 24 hours. A total of 79 relief camps and distribution centres are currently operating across five districts.

Article Title: Lok Sabha inquiry panel indicts ex-HC judge Yashwant Varma in cash-at-home case

NEW DELHI: A Lok Sabha inquiry committee on Wednesday indicted former Allahabad High Court judge Yashwant Varma in the cash-at-home case.The panel found Justice Varma’s explanation for the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory". Its report, tabled in both Houses of Parliament, said all three charges against Varma were proved.The committee said the charges are threefold - firstly, discovery and possession of unexplained Indian currency notes within official premises; secondly, failure to preserve and causing interference with material evidence; and thirdly, furnishing evasive and misleading explanations.The committee examined documentary and electronic material and recorded evidence from witnesses. It also noted that Varma was given an opportunity to respond to the charges and present his defence."The statement of grounds accompanying the charges records the occurrence of fire, discovery of cash, location of the storeroom within the Government-allotted residence, the alleged conduct after the fire, and the explanation offered by the Judge," the inquiry report said."Article I is proved. Substantial unexplained Rs 500 denomination currency notes were found in the storeroom situated within the official residential premises at 30, Tughlaq Crescent, New Delhi.The Judge failed to furnish a satisfactory explanation regarding the presence, source or ownership thereof," it said.On the third charge, the committee said Varma’s explanation, including his March 22, 2025 response and subsequent statements, did not demonstrate the "candour, transparency and institutional responsibility" expected in the circumstances. It remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against evidence from independent officials and other corroborative material.A large amount of unaccounted, partially burnt cash was discovered in the outhouse of Varma’s official residence following a fire in March 2025. The discovery triggered allegations of judicial corruption, which Varma denied.Following an in-house inquiry ordered by the then Chief Justice of India, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla constituted a three-member panel headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar under the Judges (Inquiry) Act. The motion for the inquiry was backed by MPs from different political parties.Varma resigned during the inquiry. It remains unclear whether Parliament will proceed with the committee’s findings, as some legal experts have argued that the Judges (Inquiry) Act can be invoked only against a serving judge.
Article Summary: A Lok Sabha inquiry committee on Wednesday indicted former Allahabad High Court judge Yashwant Varma in the cash-at-home case. The panel found Justice Varma’s explanation for the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory"

Article Title: How Corporate India Is Investing In Climate & Environmental Resilience
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For years, environmental CSR in India was largely associated with tree plantation drives, cleanliness campaigns and occasional conservation projects. While those initiatives continue, companies are increasingly directing their CSR efforts towards something far more strategic. They’re strengthening climate resilience, securing water resources, promoting circular use of materials, and helping communities adapt to a warming world.The change reflects a growing realisation that environmental sustainability is no longer just about protecting nature. It is about protecting livelihoods, businesses, and the economy itself.Climate change is already affecting water availability, agriculture, supply chains, and industrial operations. As these risks intensify, Corporate India is beginning to see environmental CSR not as philanthropy but as an investment in long-term resilience.The scale of the challenge is enormous. India's draft Climate Finance Taxonomy estimates that the country will require around $2.5 trillion (Roughly an estimated Rs 2,50,00,000 crore or Rs 250 trillion) to meet its climate commitments by 2030, while climate adaptation alone could require investments of nearly Rs 56.7 trillion during the same period.These figures underline why resilience has become a business imperative as much as an environmental one.Increasingly, companies are aligning their CSR programmes with this new reality. Water has emerged as one of the biggest priorities.According to the Central Ground Water Board, India extracts 245.6 billion cubic metres (BCM) of groundwater annually, with 751 assessment units already categorised as over-exploited, 206 as critical and another 711 as semi-critical. Agriculture accounts for 87% of groundwater extraction, making water scarcity a concern that extends far beyond farms to industries, cities and supply chains.For CSR programmes, this has meant a shift from isolated water projects towards landscape-level interventions. Infosys, for instance, reports creating 40 lakes across its campuses with a combined rainwater storage capacity of 430 million litres, supported by 409 deep injection wells and complete recycling of wastewater.UltraTech Cement says its operations became 4.9 times water positive during FY2024-25 through rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, watershed management and recycling initiatives. Hindustan Zinc reports achieving 3.3 times water positivity while targeting a 50% reduction in freshwater consumption by 2030. ITC, meanwhile, has expanded watershed restoration and river basin stewardship programmes alongside improvements in water-use efficiency.The common thread running through these initiatives is that they benefit both communities and businesses. Restoring watersheds improves groundwater availability for nearby villages while also reducing water-related risks for industrial operations. Wastewater recycling lowers pressure on freshwater resources while helping industries operate more sustainably.The focus is also widening beyond water. Another emerging area for CSR is the circular economy, where companies seek to minimise waste and maximise the productive use of resources. Rather than viewing waste simply as something to be disposed of, businesses are increasingly investing in recycling, reuse and resource recovery.India's policy framework now covers plastics, batteries, e-waste, waste tyres, construction waste and several other waste streams under Extended Producer Responsibility rules. As of March 2026, registered recyclers had processed 417.6 lakh metric tonnes of waste, generating nearly 342 lakh metric tonnes of EPR certificates. The government has also introduced a Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme to promote recycling of critical minerals such as lithium, nickel and cobalt.Corporate initiatives are increasingly reflecting this transition. Tata Steel reported recycling around 4.2 million tonnes of scrap during FY2024-25. Infosys diverted 98% of its waste away from landfills, while Hindustan Zinc is working towards achieving near-zero waste to landfill by 2030 through greater reuse and recycling. These examples demonstrate how environmental investments can reduce raw material consumption, lower disposal costs, and improve resource security.CSR is also beginning to support innovation rather than only funding conventional projects. Technology-led solutions are emerging as an important area of investment. Digital Paani, featured in NITI Aayog's Frontier Tech Repository, uses Internet of Things-based automation to optimise wastewater treatment plants. The platform has been deployed at more than 40 facilities, treating over 90 million litres of wastewater every day.In agriculture, Kheyti's "greenhouse-in-a-box" model has demonstrated how climate-smart farming can improve resilience. According to the study cited in the report, participating farmers recorded a 73% increase in income, 58% lower crop losses, 67% lower water consumption, and significantly lower fertiliser use. Satellite-enabled platforms such as SatSure are also helping govts, financial institutions and agribusinesses assess climate risks and improve decision-making using artificial intelligence and Earth observation data.The evolution of environmental CSR reflects a broader shift in corporate thinking. Earlier, environmental spending was often evaluated through the number of trees planted or awareness campaigns organised.Today, companies are increasingly asking whether their investments improve water security, strengthen ecosystems, reduce resource consumption, and help communities withstand climate shocks.The approach also aligns more closely with business priorities. Healthier watersheds mean more reliable water supplies. Circular resource use reduces dependence on virgin materials. Climate-resilient agriculture strengthens rural livelihoods while improving supply-chain stability. Investments in environmental resilience, therefore, generate benefits that extend beyond compliance or corporate reputation.
Article Summary: Companies are increasingly directing their CSR efforts towards something far more strategic. They’re strengthening climate resilience, securing water resources, promoting circular use of materials, and helping communities adapt to a warming world. The change reflects a growing realisation that environmental sustainability is no longer just about protecting nature.

NEW DELHI: DMK on Wednesday supported the Tamil Nadu government’s resolution opposing the Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise, with Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin saying the state’s representation in the Lok Sabha should not be reduced.He said the number of Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu should not be reduced in the name of delimitation and called for the exercise to be deferred for 25 years."In the name of constituency delimitation, the number of Members of Parliament should not be reduced. Our stand is that constituency delimitation should not be carried out for the next 25 years. We welcome the resolution on the 33% reservation for women. Our firm stand is that Tamil Nadu should not be affected by constituency delimitation. The movement that first told India what the impact of delimitation would be is the DMK," Udhayanidhi added.The development comes after Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution in the state Assembly opposing the Union government’s proposed delimitation exercise.Speaking in the assembly, CM Vijay also called for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections based on the existing 543 constituencies."The 33% reservation for women should be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections itself, based on the existing 543 constituencies. The 33% reservation for women should not be delayed any further. In Tamil Nadu, more women have voted than men. Providing reservation for women is not a concession; it is a matter of social justice. The 33% reservation for women must be implemented without any further delay," he said.The resolution seeks to safeguard the political representation of southern states, particularly Tamil Nadu, arguing that their success in controlling population growth should not result in reduced representation in Parliament."All the states including Tamil Nadu and the people / elected representatives of the union territories have not had their population counted for more than 50 years. The next census to count the population was supposed to be held in 2026. Therefore, since the delimitation of constituencies has not been carried out for the last 50 years, based on the 2011 population census, the constituencies should be delimited and the number of Lok Sabha and Assembly members should be increased from 550 to 850 by bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill," the resolution stated.The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, proposing to increase the strength of the Lower House to 850 seats and expedite the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill passed in 2023. However, the Bill failed to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting and was not passed.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed the proposed delimitation exercise and called for an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats. The Opposition has also demanded that women's reservation be delinked from delimitation.
Article Summary: DMK supports Tamil Nadu government's resolution opposing Centre's proposed delimitation exercise. Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin says state's representation in Lok Sabha should not be reduced. Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution in the state Assembly opposing the Union government's proposed exercise.
