NEW DELHI: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry, even as its total receipts between the date of announcement and completion of these polls stood at Rs 207.1 crore.According to Congress's election expenditure statement for the five state/UT polls, filed on July 31 with the Election Commission, the party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft between March 15, 2026, when the elections were announced, and May 6, 2026, when they had concluded.The Congress's full poll expense statement shows its total opening balance of cash in hand (including at the level of its central headquarters and the state/district/local level units of the 5 states/UTs) at Rs 22.9 crore and its cash in bank at Rs 146.1 crore. At the end of the polls, its cash in hand was marginally lower at Rs 22.6 crore while its bank balance had declined by 45% to Rs 80.6 crore.On the expenditure side, the party declared a total spend of Rs 143 crore on general party propaganda and Rs 105.6 crore on candidates. The latter includes Rs 95.5 crore given by the party as lump-sum payments to its candidates across the five poll-gone states/UT; while the central party headquarters bore Rs 95.3 crore of expenditure under this head, the state/district/local units disbursed only Rs 23 lakh among the candidates.Expenses on virtual campaigns through social media platforms and applications were declared at Rs 6.8 crore.Over Rs 3.2 crore was spent by the Congress on publicising the criminal antecedents of its candidates.As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements, covering print and electronic space, bulk SMS, cable TV, websites and TV channels. Another Rs 8 crore funded public meetings, processions and rallies, while Rs 11.5 crore was spent on badges, posters, cutouts, hoardings etc and nearly Rs 2 crore on miscellaneous propaganda items.Poll surveys and campaigns for the five assembly elections cost the Congress Rs 4.8 crore.A total Rs 23.5 crore was spent by the grand old party on the travel and lodging of its star campaigners (Rs 21.8 crore) and other leaders. The aircraft and helicopters were sourced from Air Charter Services Pvt Ltd, Aircab Aviation, A R Airways, GMP Air Charter, Lima Tang Aviation Service, Devigo Data Systems and Global Vectra.The Congress's central headquarters routed Rs 83.2 crore of its lump-sum payments to candidates through the state/UT units; with Kerala unit getting the largest share at Rs 55.1 crore, followed by Puducherry (Rs 10 crore), West Bengal (Rs 9 crore), Tamil Nadu (Rs 7.1 crore) and Assam (Rs 2 crore).The Congress-led UDF seized power in Kerala, but the party or its alliances performed poorly in other states, managing 21 seats in Assam, 6 in Puducherry and 2 in West Bengal, while drawing a blank in Tamil Nadu.
Article Summary: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections. The party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft. As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements.

NEW DELHI: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan on Wednesday flagged off a “Har Ghar Tiranga” bike rally in the national capital ahead of Independence Day celebrations on August 15.The rally, organised as part of the ongoing “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign, saw participation from MPs of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and a large number of supporters carrying the national flag. The rally is scheduled to cover the stretch from Bharat Mandapam to Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium.Addressing participants, Radhakrishnan noted that the various activities organised under the campaign may differ in form but carry the same sentiment of national belonging.“In Tiranga Yatra, bike rallies, cultural programmes, the activities are different but the sentiment they carry is the same, that is the collective sense of belonging... I urge each one of you to actively engage in this campaign and inspire every citizen to hoist the Tricolour with pride,” ANI quoted him as saying.The vice president also emphasised the unity of the country, declaring, “Bharat is one, and it will be one forever.”He paid tribute to Pingali Venkayya, who designed the national flag, and recalled Hansa Mehta, who led a group of 72 women who presented the first National Flag of independent India to Dr Rajendra Prasad, the country’s first president.Several NDA MPs attended the rally. BJP MP Tarun Chugh highlighted the enthusiasm of young people and their resolve to contribute towards the goal of a developed India.“Under the leadership of PM Modi, the youth have come out today with the resolution of ‘Viksit Bharat’. Tiranga is the pride of India. Under PM Modi, India will realise the resolve to become a developed India,” Chugh said.Union minister of state for Home Nityanand Rai highlighted the significance of the national flag, describing the Tricolour as a sentiment deeply connected with the country and its people.“The Tiranga is our pride, and it is more precious to us than our life,” Rai said.BJP MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri pointed to the participation of a large number of MPs in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for the Tiranga Yatra.“In response to PM Modi's call, a large number of MPs are joining this Tiranga Yatra today, and the Vice President will inaugurate this Tiranga Yatra. The journey will go from Bharat Mandapam to the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, and a spectacular celebration is visible here,” Bidhuri said.The “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign is being held across the country ahead of Independence Day, encouraging citizens, public representatives and organisations to display the national flag.The Delhi rally is part of a series of programmes being organised in the capital to mark Independence Day, with the Tricolour at the centre of celebrations aimed at strengthening the sense of unity and national pride.
Article Summary: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan flagged off a 'Har Ghar Tiranga' bike rally in Delhi. The rally saw participation from MPs of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and a large number of supporters carrying the national flag. The Delhi rally is part of a series of programmes being organised in the capital to mark Independence Day.

Article Title: 'Much more to this than meets the eye': Rahul targets PM Modi after US court drops case against Adani
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday reacted sharply to Gautam Adani 's acquittal by a US court and targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development.In a post on X, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said, "There is much more to this than meets the eye. A compromised PM was forced to sell India’s interest. India is paying a huge price. "A US federal judge in New York on Monday dismissed the nearly two-year-old criminal case against Adani and the other accused. The US Department of Justice had sought dismissal of the charges, citing six “overlapping bases”, including that the case involved foreign conduct, India had not found “actionable misconduct”, no money had been lost on securities issued and there were “extraordinary proof problems”.The case, filed in November 2024, accused Adani, his nephew Sagar Adani and six others of conspiracy to bribe Indian government officials to secure a solar power contract. The Adani Group had denied the allegations and said its companies and executives had acted in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.Judge Nicholas Garaufis had earlier questioned the DOJ's decision to drop the case and sought further explanation for the move.The DOJ had argued that the defendants were foreign nationals who had never appeared in the US and were unlikely to do so.Adani, meanwhile, welcomed the court's decision, saying: “Throughout this challenging period, our faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering. My deepest gratitude to those who never lost faith in us, in the system and in India’s capacity for justice,” according to the supplied text.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday reacted sharply to Gautam Adani's acquittal by a US court. He targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development. A US federal judge in New York on Monday dismissed the nearly two- year-old criminal case against Adani and the other accused.

Article Title: Oregon's Siletz Bay is restoring 37 acres of tidal wetland this summer, digging new channels where more than a century of diking turned marsh into pasture
Article Text:
Drift Creek Unit of Siletz Bay National Wildlife (Image Credit: Wikipedia)

How the wetlands changed

New channels reshape the landscape

From construction to a living wetland

Oregon's Siletz Bay is undergoing a major wetland restoration effort this summer, with crews working to bring back natural tidal flows to land that was dramatically altered by more than a century of diking and land conversion. According to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the project is restoring 37 acres of wetlands in the Drift Creek Unit of Siletz Bay National Wildlife Refuge, including by filling old drainage ditches and digging new tidal channels. The work is intended to improve habitat, water quality and flood resilience while creating better conditions for fish and other wildlife.The lower Drift Creek floodplain was once a complex coastal landscape made up of tidal marshes, scrub-shrub areas, spruce swamps and winding channels that carried water toward Siletz Bay. Over time, however, people changed the landscape through diking and land conversion.The dikes restricted the movement of tides, while drainage and other alterations transformed large portions of the historic wetlands into pasture. Natural channels gradually filled with sediment, leaving the floodplain far less connected to the tidal system than it had been in the past.The loss of these natural connections also affected the floodplain's ecological functions.Tidal wetlands provide habitat for fish and wildlife and help move water and nutrients through coastal ecosystems. The current restoration project is designed to reverse some of those changes by reconnecting historic floodplain surfaces and allowing tidal processes to return.Through the end of August, heavy equipment including excavators and trucks will be working across the 37-acre restoration area. Crews are filling old linear drainage ditches and excavating new tidal channels designed to resemble the pathways that once carried water through the floodplain. The project also involves placing large pieces of wood in the landscape. These structures can provide shelter for young fish while eventually becoming part of the wetland's natural habitat structure. Crews are also regrading low areas so different parts of the floodplain can reconnect with one another.The work is expected to change how water moves through the site. Instead of being confined by old drainage systems and dikes, water will be able to spread across the restored floodplain. This will help reduce flooding while allowing wetlands to perform their natural functions.The restoration is also expected to help filter sediment and nutrients from upstream flows, contributing to better water quality. For fish that depend on estuarine environments, the changes can create safer areas for movement and additional feeding habitat. Young coho and Chinook salmon, steelhead and cutthroat trout are among the fish expected to benefit, along with smaller marine species that use the estuary for shelter.The restoration will not end when the excavators leave. Once the heavy construction work is completed, the landscape will continue changing as tides, rainfall, plants and wildlife begin interacting with the newly created channels and floodplain. By fall, crews plan to plant and seed native wetland species. These will include sedges, rushes, salt-tolerant plants and coastal spruce. Over time, the vegetation is expected to help rebuild the structure of the marsh and provide additional habitat.The project is part of a larger, multi-year restoration effort rather than an isolated construction project. A first phase was completed in 2023, restoring 41 acres of former tidal wetlands east of Drift Creek Road. That phase included lowering old dikes, creating more than a mile of new tidal channels, installing large wood structures, building habitat mounds and removing aging infrastructure. Since then, native marsh and scrub-shrub vegetation has begun returning, while rare spruce swamp habitat has also started to regenerate.Several organisations are involved in the broader effort, including the MidCoast Watersheds Council, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's Oregon Coast National Wildlife Refuge Complex, Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife, Bureau of Land Management, Wild Salmon Center, Lincoln Soil and Water Conservation District, Wolf Water Resources and the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians.The goal is ultimately to allow the floodplain to function more like a natural tidal wetland again. As the new channels fill with water and native vegetation takes root, the landscape will gradually become more capable of supporting fish, wildlife and plants while helping manage water and improve coastal ecosystem health.For people travelling along U.S. Highway 101 near the refuge, the site will initially be marked by excavators and restoration crews. Once the machinery leaves, the restored landscape will continue developing with the seasons and tides.
Article Summary: Oregon's Siletz Bay is undergoing a major wetland restoration effort. Crews are working to bring back natural tidal flows to land that was dramatically altered by more than a century of diking and land conversion. The work is intended to improve habitat, water quality and flood resilience while creating better conditions for fish.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.
Article Summary: Gautam Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive. He has more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting. His appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.

Article Title: In 2020, Minnesota funded a $1.918 million Shell Rock River habitat program; by 2025, it had protected or restored 588 acres
Article Text:
Shell Rock River Watershed District (Image Credit: www.shellrock.org)

A habitat program takes shape

Three properties protected

Wetlands and prairie restored

More acres than planned

A longer-term conservation effort

In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report from the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, the program ultimately protected, restored or enhanced 588 acres of habitat in the Shell Rock River watershed, exceeding its original goal of 483 acres.The funding was provided under Minnesota Laws 2020, with the appropriation directed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an agreement with the Shell Rock River Watershed District. The funding was intended to support land acquisition as well as the restoration and enhancement of aquatic habitat within the watershed. The program focused on several types of conservation work, including acquiring properties, restoring wetlands and improving aquatic habitat. The projects were selected using conservation planning and monitoring intended to identify areas where habitat improvements could provide significant benefits.The Shell Rock River Watershed is a shallow-lake system that supports fish, waterfowl and other wildlife. According to the final report, restoration projects were targeted at addressing habitat degradation and improving conditions for native fish, waterfowl and wildlife.One part of Phase IX involved acquiring three properties: the Glenville Property, the Bancroft Property, and the Church Lake Property. The District closed on the Glenville Property in March 2021 and the Bancroft Property in September 2021. For the Church Lake Property, the District transferred the deed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources in December 2024 after acquiring and restoring the parcel.The final report says these acquisitions contributed to the program's permanent protection of 218 acres. Another 370 acres of habitat and wetlands were enhanced or restored through the program. Together, those accomplishments contributed to the reported total of 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.The program included several restoration projects beyond property acquisition. The Bancroft Wetland Restoration was initiated in 2020, with construction beginning in June 2024 and largely completed by the fall of that year. Additional seeding work was completed in spring 2025. Another project focused on Panicum Prairie, where habitat enhancement work was carried out across 300 acres. The project involved native prairie vegetation and was substantially completed in February 2025, with final work completed in May.The program also supported the Fountain Lake In-Lake Habitat Project. Work included additional rock reefs and rock boulder clusters intended to improve fish habitat. The report notes that Phase IX funds were used to expand the scope of this work after the District determined additional funds were available. These projects addressed different parts of the watershed's ecosystem, from wetlands and prairie habitat to aquatic areas. The broader aim was to improve habitat conditions while protecting areas that could provide long-term benefits for wildlife.The program's original accomplishment plan called for 483 acres. By the end of the project, the final total had reached 588 acres, 105 acres more than initially planned. The report attributes the increase to the addition of the In-Lake Habitat Project and the Church Lake Property to Phase IX.According to the report, all grant funds were spent. The final grant expenditure remained $1.918 million, while the program's final total including leverage was $1.9479 million.The work is intended to continue beyond the end of the grant. The Shell Rock River Watershed District relies on multiple funding sources, including a local option sales tax, local levy and public funding, to maintain conservation projects. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources will also maintain the Church Lake Property, which it owns.The program's results illustrate how a single state-funded conservation effort can combine land protection, wetland restoration, prairie enhancement and aquatic habitat improvements. Rather than focusing on one habitat type, Phase IX combined several projects across the Shell Rock River watershed. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored. The completed work represents a combination of permanent land protection and habitat improvements designed to support Minnesota's fish, waterfowl and wildlife over the long term.
Article Summary: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.

Article Title: It's one year to Intel becoming a 'US government company', what has this meant for the chip giant
Article Text:
What government ownership means for Intel: Some good and some not-so-good things

The US government became the largest single shareholder in Intel on August 22, 2025, after announcing an $8.9 billion agreement to acquire a 9.9% equity stake (433.3 million shares) in the company. It's been almost a year since then. In what can be called as an unprecedented shift in the US industrial policy, the federal government acquired an approximate 10% equity stake in Intel Corporation, instantly becoming the semiconductor giant’s largest single shareholder.The transaction is part of a broader, sweeping initiative in which Washington is taking equity positions in 30 publicly traded companies spanning key economic sectors. By taking a direct ownership position in Intel—a flagship U.S. chipmaker with a market capitalization of approximately $491.9 billion—the government is signaling a fundamentally new approach to supporting and securing critical national technology infrastructure. Intel forms a key piece in the administration’s effort to restore the U.S.’s domestic manufacturing capacity. Earlier this year, the US President Donald Trump said that he should have asked for a bigger stake in Intel given its newfound success.“I said, ‘Give the country 10% ownership for free in Intel,’” Trump told Fortune Magazine in a May interview. “(Tan) said, ‘You have a deal.’ I said, ‘S—, I should have asked for more.’”The move marked a transformative moment for Intel as it works to execute a turnaround focused on next-generation AI architecture and contract foundry services. As the company competes against global heavyweights like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) and Nvidia, a backed-by-Washington status could serve as a powerful differentiator.For government agencies and defense contractors with sensitive computing workloads, a federally backed domestic supplier offers crucial supply-chain security and geopolitical reliability. The government's backing strengthens Intel’s core narrative: Positioning itself as a trusted, long-term provider of critical compute infrastructure where supply chain resilience is paramount.However, the unprecedented ownership structure has immediately raised concerns among Wall Street analysts and corporate governance experts. Government involvement introduces novel questions regarding potential political interference, regulatory conflicts of interest, and capital allocation.Intel is already navigating significant execution risks, including massive capital expenditure plans and a recent $20 billion share offering. Investors worry that sovereign ownership could slow down decision-making, entangle the company in bureaucracy, or force policy-driven trade-offs at the expense of shareholder returns.Industry observers note that the federal intervention in Intel could set a wide-reaching precedent. As governments worldwide rush to secure domestic hardware capacity for artificial intelligence, Washington's move may herald a permanent shift toward state-backed corporate partnerships across the broader AI infrastructure landscape.
Article Summary: The US government became the largest single shareholder in Intel on August 22, 2025. Washington announced an $8.9 billion agreement to acquire a 9.9% equity stake in the company. The move marked a transformative moment for Intel as it works to execute a turnaround.

Article Title: Gates Foundation donates $540 million grant to University of Washington for research on…
Article Text:
Gates Foundation makes one of its biggest investments in health research

Gates Foundation's $540 million grant to expand health research

Long partnership between Gates Foundation and IHME

The Gates Foundation has announced a $540 million grant to the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington, marking one of its biggest investments in health research. As reported by Fortune, the 10-year funding will help expand global health data and research used by governments and policymakers to respond to disease outbreaks and improve healthcare. The donations come as the US government continues to reduce funding for scientific research, public health, education and other programmes, the report says, adding that the billionaire philanthropy is increasingly filling gaps left by federal funding cuts in the US.Gates Foundation's $540 million grant will allow IHME to expand its Global Burden of Disease study, which measures diseases, injuries and health risks across the world. According to the foundation, the project will increase its coverage from about 925 locations to nearly 5,000, giving governments and researchers more detailed local health data to support policy decisions.“Reliable and independent evidence can mean the difference between reacting to a health crisis after it has taken hold and acting early enough to change its course,” said Dr.Christopher J.L. Murray, IHME director and professor of health metrics sciences.“This investment will allow us to provide high-quality evidence at a much more local level and help leaders understand not only where health is improving or worsening, but which decisions can make the greatest difference for people,” he added.The latest funding builds on a long relationship between the Gates Foundation and IHME. The foundation provided the original funding to establish the research institute at the University of Washington in 2007. Since then, IHME has become one of the world's leading sources of public health data and disease research.Gates Foundation to shut down operations by 2045Gates Foundation has previously announced plans to wind down operations by 2045 and significantly increase its charitable spending over the next two decades. Earlier this year, the foundation said it would distribute $9 billion in 2026 while reducing its workforce as part of preparations for its planned closure. Bill Gates has also pledged to give away almost all of his wealth, with the foundation planning to spend more than $200 billion by 2045.
Article Summary: The Gates Foundation has announced a $540 million grant to the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington. The 10-year funding will help expand global health data and research used by governments and policymakers. The donations come as the US government continues to reduce funding for scientific research, public health, education and other programmes.
